claim: Given a fresh disposable two-module Python repository whose two imported pure one-argument boundary predicates use strict comparisons where the declared behavior is inclusive, and a visible test whose first failed assertion requires both boundary edits, the bounded model-free coupled repair loop returns exactly one candidate patch per module that changes the two comparisons, passes two verification replays, restores every source byte after search, and satisfies the independent inclusive-boundary behavior on unseen values.
scope_limits: NO arbitrary Python repair, multi-hunk semantic synthesis, or hidden-requirement guarantee
NO more than two source modules, one simple comparison per module, or any source imports
NO candidate promotion, source write, merge, benchmark, FrontierCode, or terminal-credit authority
NO claim that the coupled search is complete beyond one localized candidate mutation per file and one pair candidate
NO non-Python, persistent-repository, network, package-installation, model, or external-capability-provider support
self_description: Measurement of a solver on instances generated after the solver was frozen, judged by oracles in separate files. authority NONE: it records what was observed on this carrier and grants no credit; only a referee-signed run on a public runner may be cited.
